artifacts.summary: Re-derives the four write-surface contracts directly against brain_server.py/repo_link.py/extract_local.py rather than trusting the dispatch's paraphrase; confirms dependency task 647's sapience-api-lib.sh and sapience-project-bind.sh as the correct reuse targets; finds that .sapience/project.json structurally cannot carry a project 'key' field (parse_link's secret-key rejection), so the repo-tagged-KO publisher must resolve the key at runtime via GET /v1/people/projects keyed on the binding's cid; flags that test-sapience-mcp-registration.sh's 7-file lockstep array for the worktree-checkout-resolution block is outside this task's file_scope and needs an explicit plan-time decision; gives concrete per-endpoint loud-failure and dry-run design recommendations for all four publishers.

memory_candidates.content: Sapience's .sapience/project.json binding file (written by sapience-project-bind.sh) stores exactly {project: <cid>, name, repo} and structurally CANNOT carry a 'key' field: repo_link.py's parse_link() rejects any dict key matching its _SECRET_KEY_RE guard, and 'key' matches that pattern. A project's short workstream key (e.g. 'oliver-ben' for cid mEdYrFW_qClSGDfx) -- the value _ko_matches_channel/channel_push_matching in extract_local.py actually compares a KO's ko['project'] field against -- must therefore be resolved at write time via GET /v1/people/projects, matching the binding's cid against that live list, never read from the local binding file.

In Sapience's brain_server.py, _ingest_kos's /ingest-kos reply shape is {ok, written, threads, gated, rejected, filtered} plus conditional set_aside/staged/switched_off/project_contributed -- there is no 'spend' field on this handler despite some task-description paraphrases listing one. Any loud-failure check against this endpoint should be written against this verified field set (matching sapience-remember.sh's existing set_aside/gated/written/ok check order), not against a paraphrased field list.

Sapience doc-version writes (POST /v1/docs/<slug>) key optimistic concurrency on base_rev (the GET's 'rev': hash+body+provenance digest) compared via doc_rev(), never on base_hash alone -- base_hash is only a secondary fallback when base_rev is empty, and literally omitting base_rev against an existing doc with a stale base_hash still triggers the 409 head_moved check. The can_edit:false branch (non-chat shared docs only) returns 202 via people_propose instead of saving directly; a shared-* slug with no existing doc 404s share_gone and can never be created via this route.
